as_told.title: Greek goddess iconography and Roman-era Latin sent up on launches

plain: The mission patches made for American space launches are said to carry Latin symbols and Greek goddess imagery, and some people in that world reportedly say these are a tribute to beings they call "the sponsors." Diana Pasulka, a scholar of religion, tells this from what her sources told her: a man she calls Tyler, who worked on launches, saw imagery he did not understand, and when she asked whether the sponsors could read Latin, people answered "absolutely." In another telling she places it in today's Space Force, the US military branch for space, and talks only about the patches, without the tribute to the sponsors.
